content.title: Chwalinska’s breakout season reaches new heights with a WTA 1000 title in Wuhan
content.description: Maja Chwalinska completed another breakthrough week in Wuhan, rallying from a set down to defeat Sonay Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 and capture her first WTA title. The Pole became just the fourth player since 2009 to win her maiden WTA title at the WTA 1000 level.

content.body:
It hadn't always been smooth sailing for Maja Chwalinska since her breakthrough at Roland Garros earlier this year, but the 25-year-old proved her run to the final in Paris was no fluke with another remarkable week in Wuhan, capturing her first career title. 

The No. 16 seed rallied from a set and a break down and faced a critical juncture at 4-all in the second set before forcing a decider. She then won the final four games -- saving three break points while serving for the match -- to defeat World No. 170 Sonay Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 in 2 hours, 43 minutes and lift the 2026 Dongfeng · Voyah Wuhan Open trophy.

Chwalinska is the fourth player on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz since the format's introduction in 2009 to win her first title at the WTA 1000 level, joining Naomi Osaka (Indian Wells 2018), Bianca Andreescu (Indian Wells 2019) and Victoria Mboko (Montreal 2025).

She is also the fourth player to win a maiden WTA 1000 title this season, following Karolina Muchova (Doha), Marta Kostyuk (Madrid) and Zheng Qinwen (Beijing). 

The title carried added significance. Chwalinska became the first left-hander to win a WTA 1000 title since Petra Kvitova in Miami in 2023 and just the third Polish player to claim a WTA 1000 title, after Agnieszka Radwanska and Iga Swiatek. She defeated Swiatek in the semifinals en route to the championship.

— wta (@WTA) October 18, 2026

content.title: Dabrowski, Stefani capture Wuhan doubles crown, third title in a row
content.description: Gabriela Dabrowski and Luisa Stefani defeated defending champions Storm Hunter and Katerina Siniakova 7-5, 6-4 to win the Wuhan Open doubles title. The victory marked the top seeds' sixth title of the season and eighth overall as a team.

content.body:
Top seeds Gabriela Dabrowski and Luisa Stefani won the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open doubles title with a straight-sets victory over third seeds and defending champions Storm Hunter and Katerina Siniakova.

In Sunday’s final, Dabrowski and Stefani broke early in the first set to build a 4-1 lead before Hunter and Siniakova fought back to level the score. The top seeds broke again in the 12th game to take the set 7-5. They broke twice again in the second set while surrendering their serve once to complete a 7-5, 6-4 victory in 1 hour, 32 minutes.

“I think matches like this are decided in a few moments and a couple of points, and we could have been set down in the first set,” Stefani said in the post-match press conference.

She pointed to a deuce point in that set when Hunter missed a backhand, and said that if the ball had gone over, the story of the match might have been different.

The pair started the second set strongly and kept giving themselves chances to break in almost every game. Against a team like Hunter and Siniakova, Stefani said, “you have to be on the whole time, or at least trying to do the right things and the good things.”

“I think I’m happy about how we finish in two sets,” she said. “A really great team and tough, tough opponents.”

Showtime doubles ⭐️ Gabriela Dabrowski & @Luisa__Stefani were electric in their Wuhan final! #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/S7IKDUYMRl

— wta (@WTA) October 18, 2026

The title was the pair's sixth of the season, following their triumphs in Dubai, Strasbourg, Eastbourne, Sao Paulo and Beijing last week. It was their eighth title overall as a team and their third title in a row. The duo improved its career tour-level win-loss record to 79-19.

For Dabrowski, it was her 26th career doubles title on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz and eighth at the WTA 1000 level. Stefani claimed her 19th career tour-level doubles title and sixth at the WTA 1000 level. The pair have also qualified for the season-ending WTA Finals to be held in Indian Wells next month.

“I think for us as a team, it’s always really important to push the back ends of draws, and we’re always trying to play a relatively full schedule, but also a smart schedule,” Dabrowski told the media when asked to reflect on their season.

She said the theme has been what their coach calls relentlessness, and that the team has done a good job of living up to it. “I’m really pleased with where we are and where our level is,” Dabrowski said. “So it’s really nice to see it pay off in results consistently throughout the season.”

The pair isn’t finished yet, though, and Dabrowski made clear their focus is still on the weeks ahead. “We still have a few more weeks to go, so we’re not done yet,” she said. “And we have more to learn and more growth to do.”

For Siniakova and Hunter, this was their ninth tour-level event as a team. They have won two titles together -- at the WTA 1000 event in Dubai in 2024 and in Wuhan in 2025 -- and now have a 30-6 career win-loss record as a pair.

content.title: Martina Navratilova at 70: Her life in photos
content.description: As Martina Navratilova turns 70 years old, we look back at a career that made her one of the most accomplished players in tennis history and one of its most respected voices.
content.body:
Martina Navratilova celebrates her 70th birthday on October 18, marking seven decades of a life lived at full throttle and offering a moment to reflect on a legacy that reaches well beyond sports.

Navratilova’s fierce serve-and-volley style and dedication to physical fitness revolutionized women’s tennis and took her to the top of the game. Off court, she has been just as impactful as a sports commentator and social advocate. Unfailingly authentic, she has been resilient in public and private -- and always worn her heart on her sleeve. 

Beyond the staggering statistics of her Hall of Fame career, Navratilova describes herself as “a bit of a geek” who can’t say no to a nice pair of sneakers. As a child growing up on the outskirts of Prague, she loved picking mushrooms in the forest, and after retiring from the WTA Tour, she took woodworking classes and earned her pilot’s license. She also admires actress Katharine Hepburn for her strength and individuality.

“Tennis has given me everything,” Navratilova has often said. In turn, she continues to inspire fans around the world. As she enters her eighth decade, we look back at some of her defining highlights.

Destiny’s child

In 1975, a teenage Martina Navratilova met immigrant Czech children while playing a tournament in Sydney, Australia. The same year, after losing in the semifinals of the US Open, she made the heartbreaking decision to defect from Czechoslovakia and seek asylum in America. “After that,” Navratilova once said, “everything is a piece of cake.”

Rivals and friends 

In 1978, at the age of 21, Navratilova defeated Chris Evert to capture the first of her record nine Wimbledon singles titles, and 18 singles majors overall -- a “bittersweet” moment given the absence of her family. The win saw her usurp Evert as WTA World No. 1 for the first time. The legendary rivals would meet 80 times in all, the head-to-head matchup landing in Navratilova’s favor, 43-37. They also became lifelong friends.

Partners in history

At Eastbourne in 1985, Navratilova and Pam Shriver were presented with a cake to mark their 100th doubles match win in a row. The most successful duo in women’s tennis history won 20 Grand Slam trophies among 79 titles together, with Navratilova pocketing a record 177 doubles titles overall.

 The long way home 

In 1986, Navratilova returned to Prague for the first time since her defection, as a member of the U.S. Fed Cup team. The Americans prevailed, to the delight of many Czech fans -- even though the home team also reached the final. Navratilova regained her Czech citizenship in 2008 and was awarded the nation’s highest civilian honor, the Order of the White Lion, in 2025.

 Family reunion

With a peerless 1,442 match-wins and 167 titles to her name, Navratilova retired from singles at the WTA Finals at New York’s Madison Square Garden in 1994. This time, her parents -- mother, Jana and stepfather, Miroslav -- could be part of the emotional occasion. “My father used to say I had a golden arm and I must use it,” she said. “If I had not gone into tennis, I would have chosen a career perhaps as an architect or engineer.”

Almost 50, still winning 

Navratilova won the last of her 59 Grand Slam titles at the 2006 US Open, partnering Bob Bryan to capture the mixed doubles. The age-defying win, just six weeks shy of her 50th birthday, was a testament to her game-changing approach to training and fitness and her close attention to nutrition.

The Czech connection

In 2013, Navratilova attended the WTA’s 40th anniversary celebrations in London, where she reconnected with Jana Novotna, one of the many Czech champions inspired by the left-hander’s example over the past 50 years. Novotna drove Navratilova to radiotherapy appointments in Paris when she was treated for breast cancer in 2010.

Out and proud

After coming out in 1981 as one of the first openly gay athletes, Navratilova became a proud and vocal advocate on LGBTQ issues, even if it cost her sponsors. In 2014 she married Julia Lemigova and became a stepmother to Emma and Victoria. Later, in 2024, the couple adopted two young boys. “Getting married and having a family has been the greatest joy,” she said.

Ambassador and survivor 

In 2018, Navratilova joined forces with fellow champions including Billie Jean King as a Legend Ambassador at the WTA Finals in Singapore. A two-time cancer survivor, she says she is “especially proud to support the work of the WTA Foundation and its ACEing Cancer initiative -- beating cancer was a huge personal win for me.”

Courtside voice

Navratilova continues in her role as an unapologetically candid and highly respected television analyst, most notably for Tennis Channel, the BBC and Sky UK. She also tours the world giving motivational speeches to corporate clients and charities. 

Return to the Hall 

In 2026, Navratilova joined the celebrations as Roger Federer was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame. For an exhibition match alongside the Swiss great against Gabriela Sabatini and Marat Safin, she donned a tennis dress she wore on tour in the 1970s.

content.body:
Twelve months ago, Elena Rybakina came to the BNB Ningbo Open needing to win the title to keep her bid of reaching the year-end WTA Finals alive. The Kazakh duly did so, a triumph that eventually propelled her into the eighth and final spot at the year-end event a short time later. 

This year, Rybakina arrives in Ningbo in a much different position, as the World No. 1 and already qualified for the WTA Finals Indian Wells -- though her Asian Swing efforts have been curtailed by an ongoing foot injury that forced her withdrawal from the Dongfeng · Voyah Wuhan Open. But Iga Swiatek and Marta Kostyuk, the No. 2 and No. 3 seeds respectively at the WTA 500 event, are still in the hunt for the final qualifying spot -- and hope to close the gap on the idle Karolina Muchova -- currently No. 7 in the Race -- with strong runs.

Below is a full breakdown of each half of the draw, including first-round matches to keep an eye on, potential semifinal showdowns and Rybakina's path to defend her title. To see the full draw, click here.

Top half

After a first-round bye, Rybakina will face either Cristina Bucsa or a qualifier in the first match of her title defense. But her road to back-to-back titles only gets more complicated from there, with No. 4 seed Iva Jovic, No. 5 seed Belinda Bencic, No. 6 seed Diana Shnaider -- and the unseeded Maja Chwalinska, Alexandra Eala, and Jasmine Paolini -- all in her half.

First-round matches to keep an eye on 

[5] Belinda Bencic vs. Jelena Ostapenko: These two players come into their fourth career head-to-head meeting at different points in the final weeks of their seasons. Since withdrawing from her slated quarterfinal match against Coco Gauff in Toronto on Aug. 11, Bencic is 1-4 -- while Ostapenko just reached the semifinals in Wuhan, where she upset both Jessica Pegula and Diana Shnaider.

Alexandra Eala vs. Diane Parry: Both young talents are looking to win their first match since the US Open. Eala will look to snap a three-match skid, while Monterrey champion Parry has also lost her last four matches.

Remaining first-round matches: Cristina Bucsa vs. Qualifier/Lucky Loser, Maja Chwalinska vs. Qualifier/Lucky Loser, Jasmine Paolini vs. Qualifier/Lucky Loser, [6] Diana Shnaider vs. Qualifier/Lucky Loser

Potential semifinal showdown

[1] Elena Rybakina vs. [4] Iva Jovic: After Rybakina beat Jovic twice last year, the American teenager could hope to show off just how much she's improved with a projected semifinal meeting against Rybakina. While Jovic did not win a set in either of those matches, she's played much more post-US Open than Rybakina -- which included a successful title defense herself in Guadalajara, as well as back-to-back Round of 16 efforts in Beijing and Wuhan.

Bottom half

The chase between Kostyuk and Swiatek will heat up in the bottom half, as players including No. 7 seed Elise Mertens, No. 8 seed Sorana Cirstea, and unseeded Ekaterina Alexandrova will be among those looking to cool off their Indian Wells bid.

First-round matches to keep an eye on 

[7] Elise Mertens vs. Leylah Fernandez: Mertens has beaten Fernandez in two of their three previous meetings -- all of which have come on hard courts. But they haven't played in more than a year -- and with both in form in the Asian Swing, a first three-set affair could be on the cards.

Sara Bejlek vs. Wang Xiyu: The first career match between these two, played this summer in Toronto, was a barnburner won by Bejlek, 6–3, 4–6, 7–5.

Remaining first-round matches: Dara Kasatkina vs. Qualifier/Lucky Loser, Guo Hanyu vs. Ekaterina Alexandrova, [8] Sorana Cirstea vs. Qualifier/Lucky Loser, Marie Bouzkova vs. Qualifier/Lucky Loser

Potential semifinal showdown

[2] Iga Swiatek vs. [3] Marta Kostyuk: The sixth career match between Kostyuk and Swiatek could be on the cards for the semifinals -- and the third this year. After Kostyuk beat Swiatek on her way to the semifinals at Roland Garros in June, Swiatek got revenge with a three-set comeback in Toronto. But the winner of this match could be in pole position to continue to challenge for a year-end Indian Wells spot, while the loser's climb in the season's final weeks will prove tougher.

content.title: Chwalinska beats Swiatek in all-Polish semifinal to reach Wuhan final
content.description: Maja Chwalinska saved two set points before overcoming Iga Swiatek in straight sets to reach her first WTA 1000 final in Wuhan. She will Great Britain's Sonay Kartal on Sunday, with both players chasing their biggest career title.

content.body:
Maja Chwalinska reached her first WTA 1000 final with a straight-sets victory over Iga Swiatek in an all-Polish semifinal at the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open on Saturday. Chwalinska will face Great Britain's Sonay Kartal in Sunday's final, with both players bidding for the biggest titles of their careers.

Although Chwalinska was the first to break serve in the opening set, Swiatek consolidated a break of her own to take a 5-3 lead. Chwalinska saved two set points in the ninth game, after which Swiatek took a medical timeout to address a leg injury.

The former world No. 1 appeared hampered by the injury after returning to the court, as Chwalinska won 10 of the next 11 games to complete a 7-5, 6-1 victory in two hours, eight minutes.

FINALIST IN WUHAN!👏 Maja Chwalinska defeats Swiatek in the semifinal! #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/AymxaASOnD

— wta (@WTA) October 17, 2026

The win levels the head-to-head record between the two countrywomen at 1-1, after Swiatek won their only previous meeting at an ITF event in Stockholm in 2016.

"From the beginning of the tournament, I kind of felt pain in my quad," Swiatek said in her post-match press conference. "I've been able to manage that day by day and we were already thinking of withdrawing after I played with Magda in the first round but I was quite able to play normal, so I wanted to push, and we knew that it's nothing like that it's gonna get worse or something, so in that case, you just need to block it out. But today was just too much, and that's unfortunate because I felt like we're playing great tennis and wanted to continue. Later on, I knew it's going to be tough to win, but I didn't want to honestly retire because wanted Maja to win it normally."

"It was such a physical match, especially the first set," Chwalinska said after the match. "She had set points, so it was very close to lose this one. I feel like what I did well is I really fought for every single ball and I could, I mean, I ran to everything I could. So I think that was crucial because I made her like, she had to put extra effort. i really hope she's going to be okay soon and hope she will qualify (for the WTA Finals)."

First top 10 win and second career final for Chwalinska

The victory also marks Chwalinska's first career win over a top-10 opponent and the biggest win of her career by ranking. She advances to her second Tour-level final, following her run to the French Open final earlier this season.

With the achievement, the 25-year-old becomes only the second player to reach her first two career WTA-level finals at a Grand Slam and a Tier I/WTA 1000 event, after Amelie Mauresmo, who reached the Berlin final in 1998 and the Australian Open final in 1999.

Chwalinska has now won 17 Tour-level matches in 2026, including 11 on hard courts. Before this season, she had won only four matches at the Tour level.

"I felt very good in Singapore already," she said. "I felt like my tennis was on a very good level there so it gave me more confidence for sure. And this one feels very special for sure. As you said, you know, you have thoughts. I'm just a human being and my brain works, I mean, too much and I have too many thoughts in my head. And so, of course, I get thoughts like maybe it's just one tournament. I don't want to have just one tournament. But I guess it's not only normal that I care. So, this one feels good."

First career meeting between Chwalinska and Kartal

Sunday's final will mark the first career meeting between Chwalinska and Kartal. Since the tournament's inaugural edition in 2014, two players ranked outside the WTA top 20 have reached the Wuhan final for the first time.

Two first-time WTA 1000 finalists, one title on the line 🏆 @MercedesBenz https://t.co/WySb2tzmLE

— wta (@WTA) October 17, 2026

"I'm expecting another tough battle as I have with every match," Kartal told the media before learning who her opponent in the final would be. "It's nice to play someone different, it's going to be a challenge regardless of who it is, and I know that. I'm going to have to bring my best level to be able to come on top of that match. So, whichever one it is, I'll be excited to play. I'm going to make sure that I enjoy every second on that court. I know it's not a kind of everyday thing to achieve this, to go this far in these events. So, regardless of who it is or the outcome, I'm going to make sure that I really relish that moment."

"I have seen a few of her matches," the Pole said looking ahead to the final. "I was very impressed about the game. She plays with a lot of variety as well so I think it could be a fun one. Definitely very challenging. Hopefully, I will recover and we'll have a great show."

content.title: Advantage Kartal or Chwalinska? Making the case for the Wuhan finalists
content.description: Maja Chwalinska and Sonay Kartal will play for the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open title on Sunday. Ahead of their final, the first WTA 1000 final for both of them, we make the case for both players.

Chwalinska vs. Kartal: Everything to know about the Wuhan final
WTA Finals flashback: How Svitolina turned a shaky stretch in Asia into the biggest title of her career

content.body:
In one of the unlikeliest WTA 1000 finals in recent memory, World No. 170 Sonay Kartal will take on Maja Chwalinska in the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open title match on Sunday.

Kartal, playing just her second WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz tournament after being sidelined with a back injury for six months, beat Jelena Ostapenko 7-6 (9), 7-6 (5) in the first semifinal on Saturday.

In the second semi, Chwalinska upset compatriot and former juniors doubles partner Iga Swiatek 7-5, 6-1.

They'll both be vying for their first career WTA 1000 title, in what will unquestionably be the winner's greatest career achievement to date.

Ahead of Sunday's final, we make the case for both players.

The Case for Sonay Kartal

Players often need time to get back into form, and regain confidence, following a lengthy stint off the court. The opposite has been true for Kartal, who has found her footing instantly and is playing as well as ever.

"I'm playing with so much confidence now," she said after her semifinal win. "I'm playing with more confidence than when I started the year, before this injury."

Kartal, who is contesting just her second career WTA final after winning her first in 2024, has won seven of eight matches since returning to the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz, and this week she's barreled her way through a potent draw. After beating Anhelina Kalinina in straight sets in the first round, she took down seeded players Belinda Bencic, Jasmine Paolini and World No. 6 Elina Svitolina. And in the semifinals against Ostapenko, a former Grand Slam champion and semifinalist here, Kartal delivered in the clutch, winning a pair of tight tiebreaks to clinch her spot in the final. She's now 13-0 this season when taking the first set.

Kartal has dropped just one set through five matches, and should come into the final more rested than Chwalinska, who has spent more time on court in Wuhan than anyone.

If she wins the title, she'll become the lowest-ranked player ever to win a WTA 1000 tournament, and she's well aware of what a title of this magnitude would mean.

"Today was a dream come true," she said after beating Ostapenko. "I've been shooting to get this far in one of these events for a very long time, and to be able to do it this fast after so long out ... it's special."

The Case for Maja Chwalinska

With her creative and varied game style, Chwalinska has been known to befuddle and frustrate first-time opponents who aren't used to her approach. She'll have that advantage against Kartal, whom she's meeting for the first time.

Unlike Kartal, Chwalinska has never won a WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz title. But she has proven that she can perform on the biggest stage, winning nine straight matches at Roland Garros to make the final as a qualifier. Kartal, on the other hand, has never won six consecutive WTA matches, something she'll need to do to secure the title in Wuhan.

Chwalinska has also proven that she can be just as effective off the clay as she is on it, a revelation during the Asian Swing. She's gone 8-2 in Asia and picked up the two biggest wins of her career by ranking, first over Iva Jovic and then against Swiatek. In the semifinal against the far more accomplished and experienced Swiatek, Chwalinska came from 5-3 down in the first set and saved a pair of set points. She took control from there, winning 10 of the final 11 games to book her spot in her second career WTA final.

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

"Great defense," Swiatek said in regard to what Chwalinska did well in their match. "She's making the opponent work, and she's being smart with just playing the ball back and waiting for mistakes."

Swiatek was very efficient against Swiatek, hitting 19 winners to just seven unforced errors. (Swiatek, by contrast, had 33 unforced errors.) With that kind of steadiness and discipline, she'll have a terrific shot to win her first title.

content.title: In Memoriam: Penny Moor
content.description: Penelope ‘Penny’ Moor, who played professional tennis in the early years of the Open Era and was a founding member of the WTA in 1973, passed away on October 8 at her home in Devon, England at the age of 75.
content.body:
The WTA is mourning the death at age 75 of Penelope ‘Penny’ Moor, who played professional tennis in the early years of the Open Era and was a founding member of the WTA in 1973. Moor passed away on October 8 at her home in Devon, England, with dear friends in her presence.  

Born in Exeter on July 7, 1951, Moor’s potential was first spotted by a coach at a holiday tennis camp. After matriculating from boarding school – her parents were innkeepers who worked difficult hours – the young Penny moved to London to join a national training squad alongside contemporaries including Corinne Molesworth and Jill Cooper.

A rangy lefthander who felt most comfortable at the net, Moor understood her place in the scheme of things at a time when Virginia Wade was the undisputed queen of British tennis. When the trailblazing promoter Gladys Heldman invited her to join the nascent Virginia Slims Circuit in 1972, the young Brit jumped at the chance.

“I just thought it was going to be a bit stagnant for me in the U.K., that I would continue to struggle,” Moor told wtatennis.com in 2023.

“I just didn’t receive the same kind of encouragement here. Even though I was lower down the ranks, Gladys was just so positive, welcoming and protective. You can do it, come on out! I was inspired by her dedication and drive… it was just mind-blowing to be in her orbit.

“I wanted to experience America, and I got in at a pretty amazing time.”

She most certainly did. Suddenly, Moor was being dressed by Teddy Tinling and attending sponsor cocktail parties around the U.S. She even met the movie star John Wayne, staying on his tennis ranch and teaching his wife to play the game.

On June 21, 1973, Moor attended the famous meeting convened by Billie Jean King at London’s Gloucester Hotel, where the WTA was formed. The following week, she achieved her best Grand Slam result with a third round run at Wimbledon, and later that summer was courtside when King faced Bobby Riggs in the Battle of the Sexes at the Houston Astrodome.

Playing Chris Evert in the first round at Eastbourne in 1974, right after the young American had won her first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros, became another treasured memory.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Elena Baltacha Foundation | Children’s Charity (@elenabaltachafoundation)

“We were housed with families then – there was lots of hospitality and a lot of camaraderie and I met a lot of lovely people” Moor said. “It felt exciting, and it felt like things were evolving.

“Nowadays it’s all aeroplanes and hotels and pressure. I feel I had the best of both worlds: I made a living, I got to see the world, and I got to compete against the best of the day. I had a great time.”

With hard graft, Moor established herself in the Top 100, but at the age of 24 she sustained a knee injury that impaired her mobility long-term and affected the trajectory of her career.

In 1980, she retired from the Tour and moved to North Carolina, where she remained for two decades. There, she worked on tennis event promotions – sometimes calling on former colleagues like King and Wade – and as a country club professional and coach at the USTA’s Regional Development and Training Center in Greensboro.

An only child, Moor returned to England in 2000 to care for her elderly mother, while parlaying her interest in antique furniture into a business, as a U.K. based agent for American purveyors of furniture, lighting and home accessories.

Later, she applied her energies to giving back, with a focus on youth mentoring, coaching and creating opportunities for disadvantaged kids and wider communities through tennis. She became a valued member of the Board of Trustees of the Elena Baltacha Foundation, named for the former British No.1 who succumbed to liver cancer in 2014. More recently, Moor engaged with WTA Foundation events, including WTA Come Play clinics conducted by Judy Murray.

“Penny cared deeply about our sport’s capacity to make a difference around the world,” said Ann Austin, executive director of the WTA Foundation. “She was rightly proud of her role as a founding member of the WTA, and the platform for positive change that is still so powerful all these years later.”

Indeed, when the WTA celebrated its 50th anniversary in 2023, Moor, who had served on the Membership and Tournament sub-committees of the fledgling organization, was an enthusiastic participant and lent her Virginia Slims dresses for display.

“Ilana and I are saddened by the passing of Penny Moor, who not only a leading British player, but was one of the brave women who were in the room at the Gloucester Hotel when the WTA was formed,” said Billie Jean King.

“Penny stayed connected to tennis throughout her life and her work with the Elena Baltacha Foundation and the WTA Foundation has opened doors for people of all ages and abilities to enjoy tennis as much as she did. She will be missed and always loved.”

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Exeter Cathedral (@exetercathedral)

This past summer, Moor enlisted American Tour contemporary Trish Bostrom to help with a community tennis initiative at Exeter Cathedral, in her hometown.

“Penny was a woman of faith,” said Bostrom, reflecting on her friend. “She was generous, kind, and hard-working – and she was very courageous in leaving England to compete on the initial Virginia Slims Circuit.

“Even at 75, she was playing tennis regularly, and she often asked me to find better players for her to hit with!”

Moor’s beloved husband, Geoff, whom she married in 2005, passed away in 2024.

content.body:
WUHAN -- When World No. 170 Sonay Kartal, who is only two tournaments removed from a six-month injury layoff, meets No. 16 seed and No. 22 Maja Chwalinska in the final of the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open on Sunday, it will be the first time since the tournament’s inception in 2014 that two players ranked outside the top 20 have played for the title.

Either way, a new WTA 1000 champion will be crowned in Wuhan. Chwalinska is seeking her first career WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz title, while Kartal is eyeing her second at tour level.

From the order of play and head-to-head history to prize money and more, here's everything you need to know about Sunday's Wuhan final.

When are the Wuhan finals?

The doubles final begins play on Center Court at 4 p.m. local time, followed by the singles final, not before 6:30 p.m.

Time conversions for singles final: NB 6:30 a.m. EST , 11:30 a.m. CEST 

How did each singles player reach the championship?

Chwalinska
First round: def. Mayar Sherif 6-3, 6-2
Second round: def. [16] Marie Bouzkova 1-6, 6-1, 6-1
Third round: def. [10] Iva Jovic 6-4, 6-1
Quarterfinal: def. Maria Sakkari 6-0, 3-6, 7-5
Semifinal: def. [7] Iga Swiatek 7-5, 6-1

With her win over Swiatek, Chwalinska has earned two top 20 wins this season. She's into her first final since her Cinderella run at Roland Garros. 

Kartal
First round: def. Anhelina Kalinina 7-5, 6-3
Second round: def. [9] Belinda Bencic 6-0, 7-5
Third round: def. [15] Jasmine Paolini 6-2, 6-0
Quarterfinal: def. [5] Elina Svitolina 2-6, 6-2, 6-4
Semifinal: def. Jelena Ostapenko 7-6(9), 7-6(5), 

Kartal is into her second career tour-level final after winning the championship at the WTA 250 at Monastir, Tunisia in 2024. Every opponent she has beaten in Wuhan is ranked within the top 50.

What are the ranking points and prize money at stake?

In Wuhan, a total of USD $4,088,211 was available in prize money, and the singles champion will receive $665,000. The finalist will take home $385,001. In doubles, the winning duo splits $195,000 and runners-up earn $110,010.

As with all WTA 1000 events, 1000 ranking points are on the table in both the PIF WTA Rankings and the Race to the WTA Finals at Indian Wells, while the runner-up earns 650 points. Any change in rank is based on how the player performs in the tournament compared to the points earned in the same week last year. 

Regardless of win or loss, Kartal is projected to improve around the top 50 in the PIF WTA Rankings, while Chwalinska is projected to be in the top 15.

Chwalinska

3: Chwalinska is just the second player to make her first two career tour-level level finals at a Grand Slam and Tier I/WTA-1000 event since the format was introduced in 1990. (Amelie Mauresmo: Berlin 1998 and Australian Open 1999; Anna Kournikova: Key Biscayne 1998 and Hilton Head 1999).

4: Chwalinska could join Naomi Osaka (Indian Wells 2018), Bianca Andreescu (Indian Wells 2019) and Victoria Mboko (Montreal 2025) as the fourth player to win their first title at the WTA 1000 level since 2009.

Kartal

3: Since the format’s introduction in 1990, Kartal is the second British player to advance to Tier I/WTA-1000 final after Johanna Konta (Beijing 2016, Miami 2017, Rome 2019).

7: After a six-month injury layoff following Indian Wells, Kartal is 7-1 in tour-level matches since returning to the WTA Tour. She advanced to the Round of 32 in Beijing

170: Among ranked players since 1990, Sonay Kartal, World No. 170, is the lowest ranked player to make a Tier I/WTA 1000 final (Jennifer Capriati reached the final as an unranked player in Hilton Head in 1990).

What they had to say?

Kartal

1. "Today was a dream come true. I've been shooting to get this far in one of these events for a very long time and to be able to do it this fast after so long out.

2. "In every match, I've kind of been the underdog in this event. I think the only pressure is kind of the pressure that I'm putting on myself, regardless of how long I spent out, I still expect to offer a good performance and very proud of what I've managed to achieve this week.

"There's a lot of first time things that I've managed to do. With each match, I've grown in confidence, and the atmosphere today was amazing."

Chwalinska

content.body:
The final WTA 1000 tournament of the season has not disappointed. 

With a shortened format, there have been a flurry of incredible matches each day, accompanied by some of the most varied, creative shot-making we've seen all season.

We've rounded up our five favorite shots from the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open through the quarterfinals. Check them out, and make sure to vote for your WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz shot of the week below.

Maja Chwalinska's pinpoint right-handed lob

Chwalinska has had one of the best weeks of her career, and proven that her game can be just as effective off the clay as it is on it.

She's hit an array of remarkable, inventive shots through her first four wins, but none have been more impressive than this. Stretched wide by Maria Sakkari, the left-handed Chwalinska had to use her right hand to keep the ball in play, and the result was a perfectly weighted lob with her non-dominant hand. She then finished off the point with a backhand winner on the line.

Chwalinska won the match 6-3, 3-6, 7-5 to advance to her first career WTA 1000 semifinal.

Jelena Ostapenko's forehand slice winner on the run

Leading 4-1, 15-0 in the second set against Diana Shnaider, Ostapenko sprinted across the court to retrieve a backhand, and responded with a running forehand slice winner down the line.

In total control, and clearly feeling her shots, on the next point she hit a return winner into the same corner, this time a backhand.

Ostapenko won 7-6 (6), 6-1 to advance to the semifinals.

Diana Shnaider's wrong-footing forehand

Just incredible stuff from both players here, in one of the most athletic and reflexive points of the tournament.

After Shnaider hit a volley off of Karolina Muchova's forehand, she won the cat-and-mouse point with a wrong-footing forehand.

Shnaider won the match 7-5, 6-3.

Jelena Ostapenko's drop shot winner on match point

Does it get more daring, and clutch, than this? On Jessica Pegula's third match point, Ostapenko stayed aggressive, hitting a barrage of forehands to keep her behind the baseline. Then she pulled the string and hit a drop shot, her first of the day, for the winner to stay alive in the match. 

Ostapenko ultimately came back to win, completing the improbable comeback 2-6, 7-6 (7), 6-3 in one of the biggest upsets of the tournament.

Karolina Muchova's leaping behind-the-back overhead

Another week, another magic trick from the audacious and endlessly entertaining Muchova.

After Caty McNally brought Muchova in with the drop shot, Muchova pushed the American into the corner with a running forehand. McNally hit a very solid backhand lob, but Muchova tracked it and won the point, as only she can, with a leaping, twisting, behind-the-back overhead.

Muchova won the match 3-6, 7-6 (1), 7-6 (4).

content.description: Iga Swiatek continued her march in Wuhan on Friday, dispatching Ann Li 6-4, 6-1 to reach the semifinals and add another achievement to her résumé. The former world No. 1 will next take on Maja Chwalinska in a historic all-Polish semifinal.

content.body:
Another day, another milestone for Iga Swiatek.

The former World No. 1 defeated Ann Li 6-4, 6-1 in 1 hour, 33 minutes on Friday night to reach her first Wuhan semifinal and become the fourth player since 2009, and the only active player, to reach the semifinals at all 10 current WTA 1000 events.

Wuhan: Scores | Order of play | Draws

There, she will face compatriot Maja Chwalinska for the first time at the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz level.

The matchup will mark the second professional meeting between the former junior doubles partners. They first met at an ITF event in Stockholm in 2016 when both were 15. Swiatek won 6-2, 6-3, and a few months later the pair finished runner-up in girls' doubles at the 2017 Australian Open.

"It's great that we have two Polish players in the semifinals. I think it means a lot to Polish tennis," Swiatek said in her on-court interview. "So hopefully it's going to be a nice match. I'm really happy for Maja. She for sure improved her game this year, so I'll be looking forward to the match."

Ready for an all-Polish semifinal in Wuhan 💪 @iga_swiatek | #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/03geanDGig

— wta (@WTA) October 16, 2026

This will be the first all-Polish semifinal at a WTA-level event in the Open Era, though Magda Linette and Magdalena Frech contested an all-Polish final in Prague in 2024.

It also marks just the second time since the tournament's inception in 2014 that two players from the same country will have met in the Wuhan semifinals, following Zheng Qinwen and Wang Xinyu in 2024.

Back-to-back-to-back straight-set wins for Swiatek

Swiatek handled business in her opening matches against Frech and Ashlyn Krueger and did much the same against Li, who arrived at the quarterfinal stage playing some of the best tennis of her career.

To Li's credit, she pushed Swiatek deep into the opening set. But the six-time Grand Slam champion navigated service games of 14 and 10 points, respectively, and saved three break points in the final game to close out the set after 56 minutes.

From there, it was smooth sailing for Swiatek, who won seven of the final eight games overall to earn her second straight victory over an American and a third consecutive straight-sets win.

Another semifinal for Iga 😮‍💨 @iga_swiatek makes it to the semifinal of a WTA 1000 for the fourth time in 2026! #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/B1q8criEOG

— wta (@WTA) October 16, 2026

Li had her opportunities, but an 0-for-3 mark on break points and 49 unforced errors -- combined with Swiatek winning 74% of first-serve points and 60% of her second-serve points -- proved too much to overcome. The defeat denied Li a spot in her first WTA 1000 semifinal.

Still, Swiatek was quick to praise her opponent. Li upset top seed Aryna Sabalenka and reached her first WTA 1000 quarterfinal this week, and she is projected to achieve a career-high ranking Monday.

"We're playing really good tennis," Swiatek said. "We [both] have a lot of top spin. I'm happy with how I adjusted to the change of rhythm. We already played this year, and I know she's not an easy opponent. She's playing really great tennis and I like her style, so I knew I needed to be at the top of my game, loosen up my hand and play fast and brave."

This is now the seventh different WTA 1000 event where Swiatek has reached the semifinals without dropping a set and the first time she has done so since winning Cincinnati last season. A victory over Chwalinska on Saturday would send her to her first Wuhan final and leave her with final appearances at all 10 current WTA 1000 events.

content.body:
We're down to the final four at the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open, and opportunity abounds for a frequent WTA 1000 champion and three players looking for their first title at that level.

The first semifinal pits a resurgent Sonay Kartal against Jelena Ostapenko, who returns to this stage in Wuhan after nearly a decade.

And in the second semifinal, the first all-Polish WTA Tour semifinal in the Open Era, Iga Swiatek will play Maja Chwalinska.

Here's what to watch for in the two intriguing matches on Saturday.

[7] Iga Swiatek vs. [16] Maja Chwalinska

Swiatek leads the head-to-head 1-0

This is a special one. Though Swiatek and Chwalinska have never played at the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz level, they have a storied history and go way back. They were doubles partners as juniors, reaching the Australian Open girls' doubles final in 2017. The year prior, they played their lone professional singles match at an ITF tournament in Stockholm, in just the second pro tournament of Swiatek's career. They were both just 15. Swiatek won that match 6-2, 6-3.

Fast forward a decade later, and Swiatek is a six-time Grand Slam champion and former World No. 1. Chwalinska, meanwhile, emerged this past summer with a stunning run to the Roland Garros final, and she's built on that result during the Asian Swing. The World No. 22 is into her second semifinal in as many months, and third overall, and will make her Top 20 debut on Monday regardless of the result against Swiatek.

Swiatek's path to the semifinals has been smooth, with straight-set wins over Magdalena Frech, Ashlyn Krueger and Ann Li. It's been less straightforward for Chwalinska, whose four wins included an upset of 10th-seeded Iva Jovic, the biggest win of her career by ranking. Her stiffest test of the week came from Maria Sakkari, who pushed her to the brink in a 6-0, 3-6, 7-5 win for Chwalinska on Friday. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Chwalinska crucially saved four of her five break points in that match, and consistently put pressure on Sakkari's serve, converting four of 15 break-point opportunities. Throughout the Asian Swing, and again on Friday, she has demonstrated that her creative, varied approach is effective off the clay.

It will surely be a tale of contrasting styles, but these players know what to expect from each other. And though the stakes are high, with a WTA 1000 final berth on the line, both are appreciative of the full-circle moment.

"I feel like I know her forever," Chwalinska told reporters, prior to knowing if she would play Swiatek or Li. "Because basically we started playing tournaments together. It would be amazing, really. I think it would be great for us, and great for Polish tennis, as well.

"It would be a great honor for me also, because she's such a great champion. She's done almost everything in our sport, so it would be a great privilege to play."

Sonay Kartal vs. Jelena Ostapenko

Head-to-head tied at 1-1

The dream week, and the dream comeback, continues for Kartal, who is playing just her third tournament after six months on the sidelines. The World No. 170 is into her first career WTA 1000 semifinal, and just the second semifinal of her career, following upset wins over ninth-seeded Belinda Bencic, 15th-seeded Jasmine Paolini and fifth-seeded Elina Svitolina, the highest-seeded player left in the draw.

Svitolina was the toughest test for Kartal. In a match that went down to the wire, the 24-year-old Brit earned her first break point of the third set on match point, at 5-4, and converted it when Svitolina's forehand sailed long. It was just the second Top 10 win of her career.

Kartal is now a perfect 12-0 this season when she takes the opening set.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

"I think these courts help my game out massively," she told reporters on Friday. "I think, despite being out for so long, I came into these events knowing how much I like the atmosphere here and the environment and the surface. So I think that definitely helps, for sure.

"...I'm playing with so much confidence now. I'm playing with more confidence than when I started the year, before this injury."

Ostapenko is also playing with tremendous confidence, evidenced by her aggressive shot-making. The World No. 34, who returns to the semis in Wuhan for the first time in nine years, has hit 138 winners through four matches, the most of any player in the tournament. Following back-to-back three-set wins over Jessica Pegula and Leylah Fernandez, Ostapenko got past 11th-seeded Diana Shnaider in straights on Friday, though she did save a pair of set points in the first set. She was overpowering yet again in that match, adding 32 winners to her tally.

Ostapenko has made three WTA 1000 finals in her career, and is looking to win her first title at that level.

Kartal and Ostapenko split their two career meetings last year, though both were on grass. Kartal hopes that the hard courts will change the equation.

"She hits a great big ball on a grass court," Kartal said, "so I'm hoping this court can slow down a little bit for me. But again, I know I'm in for a good battle."

content.title: Chwalinska edges Sakkari in Wuhan thriller to make third WTA semifinal
content.description: Maja Chwalinska showed both creativity and grit to defeat Maria Sakkari in the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open quarterfinals advancing to her third career tour-level semifinal, second of the Asian Swing and first on outdoor hard courts.
content.body:
Roland Garros finalist Maja Chwalinska will make her Top 20 debut on Monday after the No. 16 seed edged Maria Sakkari 6-0, 3-6, 7-5 in a 2-hour, 35-minute barnburner on Friday to make the final four at the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open.

It will be the third tour-level semifinal, and first on outdoor hard courts, of Chwalinska's career. Two of those semifinals have come in the past month, following her run to the last four in Singapore. The Pole has used her Asian Swing debut to demonstrate that the creative game style that enthralled fans during her Parisian breakthrough can be just as effective away from clay. So far on the continent, she's compiled a 7-2 record, including her first pair of Top 20 wins.

Chwalinska to face Swiatek for first time 10 years

Chwalinska will get the chance to extend that further when she takes on childhood friend, former junior doubles partner and Polish compatriot Iga Swiatek in the semifinals. It will mark the first time that two Poles have faced each other in the semifinals of a WTA 1000 event.

"I feel like I know her forever," Chwalinska said. "Because basically we started playing tournaments together. It would be amazing, really. I think it would be great for us, and great for Polish tennis as well. It would be a great honor for me also, because she's such a great champion. She's done almost everything in our sport, so it would be a great privilege to play."

Together, Chwalinska and Swiatek won European Junior Championships doubles crowns at both U14 level (in 2015) and U16 level (2016), and were the 2017 Australian Open girls' doubles runners-up to Bianca Andreescu and Carson Branstine.

Against each other, they first played in 2014 at a U14 event in Opalenica, Poland, with eventual champion Swiatek winning 6-1, 6-4 in the quarterfinals. Their only professional meeting came two years later, in the second round of the 2016 Stockholm W10 -- Swiatek's second ever pro tournament. She was the winner again, 6-2, 6-3, but fell in the next round to Kristina Schmiedlova.

Familiar foe Sakkari brought familiar fight to Chwalinska

In the previous round, Chwalinska had dismantled 18-year-old Iva Jovic's game, delivering a masterclass in variety to win nine of the last 10 games. She picked up where she left off against Sakkari, skilfully out-manoeuvring the Greek player and dropping just one point behind her first serve. The left-handed Chwalinska even pulled off a remarkable right-handed lob, stretched far out wide by Sakkari's hefty attempted one-two punch.

Having to use her non-dominant arm didn't hamper Chwalinska's touch in the slightest: the lob was pinpoint perfect, and an effective reset of a rally she ultimately claimed with a succession of backhand winners.

The 25-year-old sealed her fifth career 6-0 set at tour level with a terrific angled pass, and held a break point in the first game of the second set -- only to send a too-cute backhand slice just wide. That was the cue for Sakkari, who had contributed 14 unforced errors in a wayward first set, to raise her level and rein her game in.

The former No. 3 struck in the very next game, putting away a forehand winner to break for the first time -- a lead she held on to throughout an impressive second set, in which she fired 17 winners to only eight unforced errors.

In the opener, Sakkari had been drawn into error by Chwalinska's variety and placement; now, she was able to stick in extended rallies, and answer Chwalinska's most creative plays with even superior ones. Twice in the fourth game, Chwalinska attempted to foil Sakkari with defensive drop shots; both times, Sakkari not only reached them but had the wherewithal to steer sliced backhand winners into the corner.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

The stage was set for a riveting decider in which both players held firm on serve through the first 11 games. Sakkari repeatedly showed her mettle when facing break points, frequently finding her best forehands and volleys to fend them off -- but she also found herself under that pressure more often than Chwalinska. The 31-year-old saved the first five break points against her in the third set (across three separate games) -- indeed, she saved 11 out of 15 during the whole match.

Chwalinska, though, had a similarly impressive rate of saving break points -- while having to face far fewer. She staved off four out of five overall, including the only one against her in the third set (with a drive volley winner in the fifth game). Repeatedly, Chwalinska was able to reset after missing opportunities on Sakkari's serve with a relatively straightforward hold.

"I was surprised about this number," Chwalinska said when asked about those break point statistics. "I didn't think about that. But I felt like in the third set, I was very solid on my serve and had a few chances on her service games -- but I mean, during the break points I think she covered them really well and honestly I couldn't do much. So I feel like I was just very solid during my service games today."

The World No. 22 had also adjusted her tactics as Sakkari had cut down her mistakes. She used her drop shot-lob combination more frequently in the decider than in the previous two sets, wheeling it out four times in one mid-set five-game stretch and winning the point every time.

In the final game of the match, Chwalinska deployed that pattern yet again to get herself into another Sakkari service game. Having worked so hard to keep her accuracy disciplined for nearly two sets, Sakkari then reverted to her first-set form in the home stretch, netting a forehand on her own game point then a short backhand down a first match point.

Despite cruising to the first set, the way in which the match played out was no surprise to Chwalinska. Having lost to Sakkari in their first meeting in 2025 Rome qualifying, she had won their third-round rematch at Roland Garros 1-6, 6-3, 6-2 -- but that had been the only set she had conceded before the final.

"It was such a physical match," she said. "Of course, I expected a very tough match against Maria. I played her twice already and both the occasions were very, very tough. It wasn't different today."

content.body:
After six months on the sidelines with a back injury that saw her ranking tumble from No. 54 to No. 170, Britain’s Sonay Kartal might have hoped to find some rhythm during her comeback, which began last month.

Instead, the 24-year-old finds herself in the final of a WTA 1000 tournament for the first time after knocking out world No. 6 Elina Svitolina 6-2, 2-6, 6-4 in the quarterfinals and Jelena Ostapenko 7-6(9), 7-6(5) in the semifinals of the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open. 

The victory over Svitolina was Kartal's first against the Ukrainian in three meetings. Both wins also extended her unbeaten record to 13-0 in 2026 in WTA-level main draws when she wins the first set. 

"I'm very proud to get through that one," she said in her post-quarterfinal press conference. "It was far from easy. I played at the very start of the year in Auckland. I know her pretty well, so I know that until the last point was played, I was never safe. I'm proud of the level that I managed to produce. And I'm very happy that I've been so consistent this week."

The win over Svitolina was Kartal’s second career victory over a top-10 opponent and her win over Ostapenko sent her into her second career WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz final. Since the format’s introduction in 1990, Sonay Kartal is now the second British player to advance to Tier I/WTA-1000 final after Johanna Konta (Beijing 2016, Miami 2017, Rome 2019).

WHAT A MOMENT 🤩 Sonay Kartal is into the final in Wuhan! #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/C6RyteZj9b

— wta (@WTA) October 17, 2026
"I think I'm just growing in confidence with every match that I'm playing"

Since returning to competition last month, Kartal has represented Great Britain in the Billie Jean King Cup and reached the third round in Beijing, where she defeated world No. 31 Wang Xinyu. She has continued that momentum in Wuhan, recording wins over world No. 48 Anhelina Kalinina, No. 9 seed Belinda Bencic and No. 15 seed Jasmine Paolini before overcoming Svitolina.

"I definitely did not think that I would find this level this fast," she said. "I think it's a bit of a surprise to me. I've had my best wins in my third tournament back. I did lose six months on the tour, but I don't feel like that when I'm playing on the court. So, for me, that's a big positive.

"I think now that I'm back, I'm just going to try and maintain this level and try and find my ceiling and see where I can get to in the next year or so."

"The biggest advice I received was don't rush it"

Kartal revealed that she had actually been ready to return in late August but chose to listen to the advice of those around her rather than rush her recovery.

“I was ready to get back kind of end of August time but I knew I was going to come back to these events," she added. "I had to try and replicate the environment of a match as best as you can in training. I don't think you can replicate it, but I didn't rush myself.

“I've got a lot of tennis years left in me, so I took advice from a lot of other players who have had lengthy injuries. I just had a great physio down here and I just trusted in her and trusted in the team that when I would get back. I didn't know that I would get back to the level that I know I can do.”

The decision to be patient was not an easy one. Kartal acknowledged the the disappointment of missing some of the sport's biggest events, including her home Slam at Wimbledon, but said she had learned to trust her support team.

“I think the biggest advice I received was don't rush it," she said. "When you're playing an individual sport, you want to get back as quickly as you can for many reasons, financially and, I love playing in these atmospheres... but I had to trust the people around me. I know I have the best in the game and at the end of the day, they know what they're doing.

"I might be stubborn and want to try and push them, but ultimately I've got to sit back and listen. It's rare as a tennis player you get six months away, so I tried to make the most of it.”
content.summary: After six months out with a back injury, Britain’s Sonay Kartal has surged into her first WTA 1000 final, upsetting world No. 6 Elina Svitolina and Jelena Ostapenko in Wuhan.

content.body:
Zheng Qinwen will miss next week's WTA 250 Kinoshita Group Japan Open in Osaka, citing a continued shoulder injury.

It's the second consecutive withdrawal for Zheng, after pulling out of Wuhan earlier this week. 

Zheng's withdrawals come on the heels of her milestone title in Beijing, where she became the first Chinese woman to win the China Open. In the main draw as a wild card, she won four consecutive three-setters before upsetting Elina Svitolina in the quarterfinals, Elise Mertens in the semifinals and Mirra Andreeva in the final. 

She spent 15 hours and 16 minutes on court during her seven matches in Beijing. That's the most time spent on court by any player at any tournament this year, and the most since Opta began tracking total time spent on court in 2023. 

It was Zheng's first career WTA 1000 title, and her first WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz title since 2024.

"Since returning from injury, I have played a demanding stretch of tennis over the past month and a half, competing at the US Open, the Billie Jean King Cup and the China Open," Zheng said in a statement after withdrawing from Wuhan. "My body is feeling very fatigued after this intense run of matches."

Since the start of the US Open, where Zheng reached the quarterfinals as a qualifier, she has won 14 of her last 15 matches, with the lone loss coming to World No. 1 Elena Rybakina. Nine of those 15 matches went to three sets.

Zheng came into the US Open ranked No. 121 in the PIF WTA Rankings, and in less than two months she's risen 98 spots, to No. 23.

World No. 68 Ashlyn Krueger has moved into the main draw in Zheng's absence.

Zheng is still scheduled to play the WTA 250 Prudential Hong Kong Tennis Open next month, one of the final two tournaments on the calendar before the WTA Finals at Indian Wells.

The Kinoshita Group Japan Open will begin on Oct. 19 and run through Oct. 25.

content.title: By the numbers: Swiatek's 150th WTA 1000 win boosts WTA Finals chances
content.description: Iga Swiatek notched her 150th WTA 1000 win Thursday night in Wuhan, defeating lucky loser Ashlyn Krueger 6-1, 6-4 to reach the quarterfinals for the second straight year. The win also strengthened her bid for a WTA Finals berth.

related.label: Career-best win sends Chwalinska into the Wuhan Open quarterfinals

content.body:
Iga Swiatek collected her 150th WTA 1000 win Thursday night in Wuhan, defeating lucky loser Ashlyn Krueger 6-1, 6-4 in 1 hour, 34 minutes to reach the quarterfinals for the second consecutive year.

Wuhan: Scores | Order of play | Draws

Among the seven players to reach the milestone since the format's introduction in 2009, Swiatek (187) did so in the fewest matches. Since 1990, she is just the third player to record at least 150 wins within her first 50 Tier I or WTA 1000 main draws, joining Martina Hingis (162) and Serena Williams (153).

The milestone also helped Swiatek gain ground in the race to qualify for the WTA Finals Indian Wells. Karolina Muchova, who currently occupies the final qualification spot, fell to Diana Shnaider earlier Thursday in the Round of 16.

"It's not easy at the end of the season, so I'm really focusing on recovering every day as much as possible," Swiatek said in her on-court interview. "But I'm happy to get some wins, because I feel like I'm playing better than at the beginning of the season, so I'm ready to push and happy to be in the quarters."

Swiatek has now reached seven WTA 1000 quarterfinals in 2026, surpassing Elena Rybakina for the most by any player this season. It marked her 32nd career WTA 1000 quarterfinal. Only Aryna Sabalenka (33) has reached more among active players.

It wasn't Swiatek's sharpest performance, but her steadiness under pressure, combined with Krueger's mounting error count, carried her to a relatively straightforward victory.

Soaring into the quarterfinals 🪽 @iga_swiatek moves past Krueger in straight sets! #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/ag2ysyCRAQ

— wta (@WTA) October 15, 2026

Here are the key numbers from Swiatek's latest victory and what they could mean for the former World No. 1 moving forward:

5: Consecutive WTA Finals appearances. The 2023 champion has qualified for the year-end championships every year since making her debut in 2021. Entering the week, she was tracking toward an alternate position, but a few more wins could further tighten the race.

7: Break points saved. Swiatek excelled in the biggest moments on serve, saving seven of eight break points. Krueger created opportunities throughout the match, but Swiatek consistently came up with timely responses to escape trouble.

9: Wins against lucky losers. As a result, Swiatek improved to 9-0 against lucky losers in her career, with eight of those victories coming in straight sets. Her only three-set win over a lucky loser came against Zheng Qinwen in San Diego in 2022.

41: WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz match wins in 2026. With two more wins in Wuhan, Swiatek has improved to 41 victories on this season. She has been particularly effective since the return to hard courts, posting an 18-3 record since Toronto.

46: Unforced errors by Krueger. The American generated more winners than Swiatek (16-9) but undermined her efforts with 46 unforced errors, 19 more than her opponent. Many of her best opportunities disappeared through self-inflicted mistakes.

Swiatek will face Ann Li, who upset top seed Aryna Sabalenka in the second round Wednesday, in the quarterfinals. Swiatek lost her only previous meeting with Li via retirement in Madrid earlier this season.

content.title: Breaking down the quarterfinal matchups in Wuhan
content.description: We're down to the final eight in Wuhan. Ann Li plays Iga Swiatek, Maja Chwalinska takes on Maria Sakkari, Elina Svitolina faces Sonay Kartal and Diana Shnaider plays Jelena Ostapenko. We break down the quarterfinal matchups.

content.body:
This time last week, only one top-five seed remained in the hunt in the Beijing quarterfinals.

The same is true this week in Wuhan, where World No. 5 Elina Svitolina is the highest-seeded player left in the field.

Unseeded Zheng Qinwen took advantage of the opportunity in Beijing, and Ann Li, Maria Sakkari, Sonay Kartal and Jelena Ostapenko will look to follow in her footsteps in the final WTA 1000 tournament of the season.

Here's everything you need to know about the quarterfinal matchups in Wuhan.

Ann Li vs. [7] Iga Swiatek

Li leads the head-to-head 1-0

Li is still riding high after upsetting World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka, the biggest win of her career. The 26-year-old American showed tremendous poise and resilience in that match, converting her 10th match point in an epic 3-6, 6-4, 7-6 (5) win. 

"I think on some of those match points I was about to lose my mind," she said after the match. "I was about to crash out."

Instead, she stayed within herself, trusted her shots and persevered. And despite all the whirlwind of emotions that accompanied that match, there was no post-Sabalenka hangover. Li took care of business again on Thursday, beating Janice Tjen in straight sets, and she's into her first WTA 1000 quarterfinal.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Swiatek, by contrast, is into her 32nd WTA 1000 quarterfinal, including seven this year. And every match from here on out carries significant weight. Not only is she playing for the Wuhan title, but she remains in contention for a WTA Finals berth. Swiatek has yet to drop a set through two matches, and she looked particularly strong on her return on Thursday, saving seven of eight break points against Ashlyn Krueger.

In their lone match on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz, earlier this year in Madrid, Swiatek retired with a gastrointestinal illness while trailing 3-0 in the third set.

[16] Maja Chwalinska vs. Maria Sakkari

Head-to-head tied at 1-1

It's been a welcome return to Wuhan for Sakkari, who last played this tournament in 2018. She's had success here before, making the semifinals in 2017, and she has an opportunity to match that result on Friday. Sakkari had one of her wins of the season in the second round, a come-from-behind upset of Marta Kostyuk, sandwiched between two straight-set wins over Donna Vekic and 17-year-old wild card Mia Pohankova. 

She'll play Chwalinska, who is having the best tournament of her career outside of her breakthrough run to the Roland Garros final. Chwalinska recovered from 6-1 down to beat Marie Bouzkova, then upset Iva Jovic 6-4, 6-1, the biggest win of her career by ranking. Chwalinska was far more consistent than the American in that match, hitting 16 fewer unforced errors.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Sakkari came from a set down to beat Chwalinska in their first career meeting, last year in Rome. Chwalinska flipped the script at Roland Garros this year, winning 1-6, 6-3, 6-2. That match is still fresh in Chwalinska's memory.

"It was an extremely hard match," she told reporters in Wuhan. "I remember that I was struggling physically. It was very hot, and Maria played amazing in the first set. I remember that. I didn't basically have any chance. So I'm expecting a very tough match again."

[5] Elina Svitolina vs. Sonay Kartal

Svitolina leads the head-to-head 2-0

Similar to Sakkari, this is Svitolina's first time in Wuhan in quite awhile. Prior to this week, she had last played this tournament in 2019, when she made the quarterfinals. She's back there again after a pair of wins over Liudmila Samsonova and Chinese wild card Guo Hanyu, the latter of whom had spent nearly six hours on court going into their match. Svitolina, who is inching her way towards a WTA Finals berth, wasn't at her best against Guo despite the 6-1, 6-4 scoreline. She made less than 50 percent of her first serves and made 32 unforced errors, though she did create 16 break points, converting seven of them.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Kartal, on the other hand, was locked in from start to finish in her third-round win over Jasmine Paolini, a clinical 6-2, 6-0 beating that took just 67 minutes. She had 14 winners to just eight unforced errors, and won the last 11 games. Playing just her third tournament following a sixth-month injury layoff, she's yet to drop a set in three matches, including another upset of ninth-seeded Belinda Bencic.

Svitolina and Kartal played at the very start of the year, in Auckland. It was a tight back-and-forth battle, with Svitolina narrowly winning 6-4, 6-7 (2), 7-6 (5).

[11] Diana Shnaider vs. Jelena Ostapenko

First career meeting

Coming into this tournament, Shnaider didn't have the fondest memories of Wuhan. She had played here twice, and lost in the first round each time. And after arriving from Beijing after reaching the doubles semifinals, she didn't have the highest hopes that this would be the year she'd turn it around.

"When I came here, I was dead mentally, and definitely wasn't expecting to do great," she said.

To her surprise, she has been great -- nearly flawless, in fact. Shnaider has won all three of her matches this week in straight sets, the last of which was a 7-5, 6-3 upset of sixth-seeded Karolina Muchova. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

She'll face Ostapenko, who has had a far more laborious path to the quarterfinals. She dropped just two games in her first-round win over Daria Kasatkina, but from there she was pushed to her limit by second-seeded Jessica Pegula. After dropping the first set 6-2, she saved three match point in the second-set tiebreak in a thrilling 2-6, 7-6 (7), 6-3 win. She went the distance again on Thursday, beating Leylah Fernandez 6-1, 1-6, 6-4. 

Ostapenko is a former semifinalist in Wuhan, reaching the final four back in 2017.

content.body:
• Svitolina will make her fourth WTA Finals appearance, and her first since 2019.

  • First mother to qualify in singles for the WTA Finals since Kim Clijsters in 2010.

The WTA on Saturday announced Elina Svitolina has qualified for the WTA Finals Indian Wells, returning to tennis' ultimate stage for the first time since 2019.

Svitolina will make her fourth WTA Finals appearance after winning the title without losing a match in 2018 and reaching the final again in 2019.

Svitolina is the first mother to qualify for the WTA Finals singles field in more than 15 years and will look to match Kim Clijsters, who won the title in 2010.

Svitolina becomes the seventh singles player to qualify for the WTA Finals, leaving one spot available. The 32-year-old will join PIF WTA World No. 1 Elena Rybakina, Indian Wells and Miami champion Aryna Sabalenka, Roland-Garros winner Mirra Andreeva, Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova and Americans Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula in Indian Wells.

Svitolina’s two titles this season -- the WTA 250 ASB Classic in Auckland at the start of the year and the WTA 1000 Internazionali BNL d’Italia in Rome -- brought her career total to 20, fifth among active players, and helped her return to the WTA Finals for the first time in seven years. She also reached the final of the WTA 1000 Dubai Duty Free Tennis Championships.

Svitolina won the WTA Finals without losing a match in 2018, making her one of only 10 players to do so since the round-robin format returned in 2003.

The WTA Finals Indian Wells features the Top 8 singles and doubles teams on the PIF Race to the WTA Finals Leaderboard (with the 8th spot going to the singles player and doubles team that have won a Grand Slam if ranked No.8 to No.20).

This showcases the world’s best singles players and doubles teams competing in a round-robin format with the singles champion lifting the WTA Finals Billie Jean King Trophy and the doubles champions earning the WTA Finals Martina Navratilova Trophy. The prestigious season-ending tournament celebrates the best of the WTA on and off the court, delivering an unrivalled fan experience that blends sport, entertainment, and culture.

Tickets are available here or this year's WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden, one of the sport's premier destinations and tournament locations.

content.body:
French Open runner-up and No. 16 seed Maja Chwalinska scored the biggest win of her career by ranking, upsetting world No. 11 Iva Jovic in straight sets 6-4, 6-1 to reach the quarterfinals at the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open.

In a matchup between two of the season's breakout stars, Chwalinska earned the decisive break in the ninth game of the first set before holding serve to take it 6-4.

With the opening set under her belt, Chwalinska dominated the second as the errors mounted for the 10th seeded Jovic. After the pair traded holds to start the set, the Pole won five consecutive games to complete the victory in 1 hour and 49 minutes.

Continues her run 💪 Maja Chwalinska makes it to the quarterfinals in Wuhan, defeating Jovic 6-4, 6-1. #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/lkSVnt2chB

— wta (@WTA) October 15, 2026

Chwalinska was the more consistent player on the day, hitting 17 winners against 15 unforced errors. Jovic struck 23 winners but committed 31 unforced errors.

"I think it was quite a solid match from my side," Chwalinska said in her post-match press conference. "Iva is an amazing player. I knew that I needed to play my best game to get a win today.

"I think we had many very challenging rallies and it was a very physical match, I think, even though the score maybe doesn't show it, but it was definitely a very hard match. Yeah, very happy about the performance."

'Definitely a moment to appreciate for sure'

Reaching the last eight in Wuhan is another milestone for Chwalinska in what has been her most successful season on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz so far, something which she acknowledges and appreciates.

"It has been a great year for me for sure," Chwalinska told the media. "Very unforgettable year. Last year I was in a different position for sure. I was probably preparing for South American clay courts tournaments at the end of the year and now here I am, so very happy, very grateful for that.

"Actually, I talked with my physio today, who is also the physio of our Billie Jean King Cup team. And we talked, I think, in April when we had a tie in Poland. I was maybe 120 [in the rankings]. You know, I'm just not feeling like I fulfilled my potential and I'm getting old. And he's here with me now, and I'm probably going to be top 20. So, it's definitely a moment to appreciate for sure."

Sakkari next; H2H tied at 1-1

She'll next face Maria Sakkari in the last eight. The Greek defeated wild card Mia Pohankova 6-1, 6-4 in another third-round match Thursday.

— wta (@WTA) October 15, 2026

This will be the third career meeting between the two players. Sakkari won the pair's first meeting in the qualifying rounds in Rome last year, prevailing in three sets. Chwalinska gained revenge with a three-set victory over Sakkari n the third round of the French Open this year.

"It was an extremely hard match," Chwalinska said while reflecting on their meeting in Paris. "I remember that I was struggling physically. It was very hot, and Maria played amazing in the first set. I remember that. I didn't basically have any chance. So I'm expecting a very tough match again. I know I repeat myself, but I really think that it's just how the tennis is. You need to be prepared all the time to give your best. So I'm definitely expecting a battle."

content.body:
WUHAN -- The past two years at the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open, Diana Shnaider's stay was short. 

She hadn't won one match in Wuhan -- both singles and doubles -- until this year's edition. With a 7-5, 6-3 win Karolina Muchova, Shnaider is through to the quarterfinals. She picked up her fourth top 10 win of her career -- three this season -- and she's into her fourth career WTA 1000 quarterfinal. All of her wins at the tournament thus far have come in straight sets.

It's been a strong year for the World No. 13, who's amassed a 32-20 record on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz in 2026. Her season has been highlighted by a semifinal runs at Roland Garros, Adelaide and Washington, and quarterfinal finishes in Toronto and Charleston, and she's maintaining the consistency into the Asian Swing. 

"It wasn't a lot of time to adjust to the new courts, new balls," Shnaider said on coming to Wuhan after reaching Beijing doubles semifinals. "It was a little bit hard just mentally that you had just one day where you can forget about tennis. And then all over again, but this is what happens when you go a little bit deeper in a tournament.

"I'm very happy that I'm in the quarters because when I just came here, I was dead mentally, and definitely wasn't expecting to do great."

Shnaider's been consistent over the last three seasons on tour, hovering in and out of the top 20. She achieved her career-high rank of No. 11 in May 2025, and she sits at No. 13 right now. Two years ago at Wuhan, she entered as No. 16 on tour. 

As her consistency has strengthened, Shnaider has also invested more into her team.

Her lead coach, Sascha Bajin, has been with her since August 2025, and now she travels more frequently with fitness coaches and rotating hitting partners. The concept of building a team has been a learning curve for Shnaider, but she's figured out the balance on what tournaments to bring a whole team vs. a reduced operation. She also has fitness coaches in select areas geographically depending where she is on tour, such as the United States.

"It takes a little bit more time to create the team around you. You need to find the right people and obviously sometime it is hard," Shnaider said. "I'm just trying to figure out what type of mindset I want to have on tournaments, off the tournaments, because everyone wants to have a success.

"Everyone wants to help you, but sometimes you understand and maybe this one is a little bit too much, maybe this one is a little bit less. So I'm just trying to find myself what I want to have on tournaments, between tournaments, before matches to what's the most comfortable for me."

The first part of the 2025 season saw fluctuation in Shnaider's team, but by bringjing Bajin on board -- and his plethora of experience -- the consistency in her team itself has fueled the strong year.

From both tactical and mental perspectives, Shnaider lauded the partnership. 

"We keep working on the court and a lot of different stuff, and I feel there is still a lot of things that we can do more and work more because work never stops. We also talk a lot about the tactics, the easier shot, the short placement and everything.

"We talk the mental side of it, like today. 'It's okay, if it's nine times deuce, but you got to go. If it's nine, it's nine. If it's five, it's five. If it's 15, 15. You're not going to let your emotions in front of you [or] get tired."

Shnaider could reach her fourth semifinal of the year, and faces the winner of Jelena Ostapenko and Leylah Fernandez in Friday's quarterfinals.
